newsitem.title: JAPAN: Suzuki Motor sees 97/98 parent oper prft Y34 bln.
newsitem.headline: Suzuki Motor sees 97/98 parent oper prft Y34 bln.

text.p: Suzuki Motor Corp said on Tuesday it forecast a parent operating profit of 34 billion yen in the year to March 1998, down 2.3 percent from the previous year.
The company, Japan's biggest maker of minicars, earlier said it expected a parent operating profit of 34.81 billion yen in 1996/97, up 2.7 percent from the previous year.
Executive vice president Yoshio Saito said: "We hope to maintain 1997/98 group profit at the same level as last year."
He did not give a specific forecast.
Suzuki said it planned capital investment in 1997/98 of 57.4 billion yen, down from 60 billion yen the previous year.
The company added that depreciation costs for 1997/98 were expected to rise to 50 billion yen from an actual 43 billion yen the previous year.

The rise in depreciation costs was partly due to the cost of developing minivehicles to meet new Japanese standards that will come into effect in October 1998. The size of minivehicle bodies will be increased under the new standards to meet safety requirements.
The company forecast its domestic minivehicle sales at 560,000 in 1997/98, down 2.7 percent from the previous year, while it expects sales of its compact cars to rise 5.3 percent to 75,000 vehicles.
It expects its total vehicle exports to rise 10.4 percent in 1997/98 to 222,000 vehicles. It forecast its overseas vehicle production in 1997/98 at 1.03 million vehicles, up 1.4 percent.
